bull.b: Sustained top-line growth with very high gross margins shows the core products generate strong incremental economics. That structural margin profile means additional revenue can flow to the bottom line as operating costs are contained, supporting durable profitability potential once fixed costs are reduced.

Multiple commercial franchises and geographic penetration reduce single-product concentration risk. Rapid Evkeeza adoption and expanding patient counts across regions indicate sustainable demand, stronger payer relationships and reusable commercial infrastructure for new launches, improving long-term revenue resilience.

bull.t: Credible path to profitability and PRV plan
bull.b: A management plan that combines disciplined expense cuts, double-digit revenue growth from existing franchises and potential launches, plus monetization of priority review vouchers if approvals occur, creates a credible multi-year path to positive operating cash flow and lower reliance on equity financing.

bear.b: A structurally weakened equity position reduces financial flexibility over months and years. Negative equity can constrain access to unsecured capital, increase cost of financing, and create investor and counterparty concerns, making funding strategic initiatives and launches more challenging without non-dilutive proceeds.

Large and persistent negative operating and free cash flows mean the company requires ongoing external funding or asset monetization to sustain operations. This structural cash burn elevates refinancing and dilution risk absent regulatory successes or material cost reductions, constraining strategic optionality.

Reliance on a small set of pivotal approvals and trial readouts creates lasting execution risk: failed or ambiguous outcomes can force new studies, delay launches, increase spend and remove expected revenue/PRV proceeds. Such binary dependencies materially impact multi-quarter funding and growth plans.
